name: Single-Leg Stand
instructions: Stand on one leg with the other foot lifted just off the floor. Hold your balance as steadily as possible.
coaching_cue: Fix your gaze on a point at eye level. Think about pressing your standing foot into the ground.
common_mistakes: Looking down, locking the standing knee, tensing up the whole body.
modification: Keep one fingertip on a wall or chair for balance support.
advanced_progression: Close your eyes or stand on a folded towel for an unstable surface.

name: Heel-to-Toe Walk
instructions: Walk in a straight line placing the heel of one foot directly in front of the toes of the other foot. Walk forward, then reverse.
coaching_cue: Keep your gaze forward, arms out to the sides if needed for balance.
common_mistakes: Looking at feet, rushing, not placing heel directly in front of toes.
modification: Walk near a wall for support if needed.
advanced_progression: Try it with your hands on your hips or eyes partially closed.

name: Lateral Band Walk
instructions: Place a resistance band around your legs just above the ankles. Stand in a quarter squat and step sideways, keeping tension on the band. Complete steps in one direction, then return.
coaching_cue: Stay low in your quarter squat the whole time — don't pop up between steps.
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, letting the trailing leg snap inward, shuffling instead of stepping.
modification: Place the band above the knees for less resistance.
advanced_progression: Use a heavier band or add a squat after every 3 steps.

name: Single-Leg Reach (Bodyweight RDL)
instructions: Stand on one leg with a slight knee bend. Hinge forward at the hips, extending the free leg behind you, and reach your hands toward the floor. Return to standing.
coaching_cue: Your body and back leg should move as one unit, like a seesaw. Keep the standing knee soft.
common_mistakes: Rounding the back, opening the hips (rotating), losing balance by rushing.
modification: Keep the back toe lightly touching the floor, or hold a chair.
low_impact_alternative: Supported version with one hand on a wall.
advanced_progression: Hold a dumbbell in the opposite hand.

name: Calf Raise
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width apart (use a wall for light balance support if needed). Rise up onto your toes as high as you can, hold for a moment, then lower slowly.
coaching_cue: Push through all five toes evenly and control the lowering phase — don't just drop down.
common_mistakes: Rolling outward on the ankles, bouncing, not using full range of motion.
modification: Hold a wall or chair for balance support.
advanced_progression: Single-leg calf raises or hold dumbbells.

name: Squat to Overhead Press
instructions: Hold dumbbells at shoulder height. Perform a squat, and as you stand, press the dumbbells overhead. Lower the weights back to your shoulders as you begin the next squat.
coaching_cue: Use the momentum from standing up to help drive the press. Keep your core tight throughout.
common_mistakes: Pressing before fully standing, arching the back at the top, rushing.
modification: Lighter weights or separate the movements (squat, then press).
low_impact_alternative: Bodyweight squat and dumbbell press done separately.
advanced_progression: Increase weight or add a single-leg stance.
